steps: Cook 200g brown rice per packet instructions (or swap half for quinoa), then divide into 5 containers.
Divide 1 cup black beans (warmed through) over the rice in each container.
Top each portion with 3 tbsp guacamole and 2 tbsp salsa.
Sprinkle 1 tbsp nutritional yeast over each bowl.
Add hot sauce to taste just before eating, keeping it separate until serving so the rice doesn't turn soggy.
Cook 200g white rice per packet instructions and divide between 4 bowls.
Peel a ripe plantain, slice into 1cm-thick diagonal rounds, and roast at 200°C for 15-18 minutes, turning once, until caramelised and soft.
Warm 1 cup black or red beans through in a small pan.
Spoon the beans over the rice, then top each bowl with roasted plantain and a quarter avocado.
Finish with a squeeze of lime and a scatter of chopped coriander.
Peel and cube 200g sweet potato, toss with a little oil, and roast at 200°C for 25-30 minutes until tender and caramelised at the edges.
Cook 100g quinoa per packet instructions and warm 150g black beans through.
Whisk together 2 tbsp olive oil, a squeeze of lime juice and a pinch of ground cumin to make the dressing.
Divide the quinoa between 4 bowls and top with the roasted sweet potato, black beans and a quarter avocado each.
Drizzle with the cumin-lime dressing just before serving.
Peel and cube 200g sweet potato, toss with a little oil, and roast at 200°C for 25 minutes until tender.
Press 150g firm tofu to remove excess water, cube it, toss with 1 tbsp tamari, and roast alongside the sweet potato for the last 15-18 minutes until golden.
Roast 1 cup mixed vegetables on a separate tray with a little oil for 20 minutes, turning once.
Divide the roasted sweet potato, tofu and vegetables between 4 bowls.
Top each bowl with half an avocado, sliced, and drizzle any remaining tamari over the top.
Marinate 120g sliced lean beef in a little soy sauce, sesame oil and minced garlic for 15-20 minutes.
Blanch the bean sprouts and spinach separately in boiling water for 1 minute, then plunge into cold water, squeeze dry, and season each with a little sesame oil and salt.
In a hot pan, sauté the carrot until just softened, then the mushrooms, then the marinated beef, cooking each separately and setting aside.
Fry an egg per portion, keeping the yolk soft.
Divide 250g cooked rice between 4 bowls and arrange the beef, spinach, carrot, mushroom and bean sprouts around the rice in separate sections.
Top each bowl with a fried egg, 1 tbsp gochujang and a drizzle of sesame oil, then mix everything together just before eating.
Press 150g tofu to remove excess water, cube it, and bake at 200°C for 20-25 minutes until golden, turning halfway.
Cook 100g soba noodles in boiling water per packet instructions, then drain and rinse under cold water to stop them sticking.
Whisk together the sesame-ginger-tamari dressing (grated ginger, tamari, sesame oil, a little rice vinegar).
Toss the noodles with shredded carrot, cabbage and half the dressing.
Divide between 4 bowls, top with the baked tofu and edamame, and finish with sliced spring onion and the remaining dressing.
Poach 150g chicken breast in gently simmering water for 12-15 minutes until cooked through, then cool slightly and shred.
Cook 100g rice vermicelli in boiling water for 3-4 minutes until just tender, then drain and rinse under cold water.
Whisk together the juice of 1 lime, grated ginger, 1 tbsp olive oil and a pinch of salt for the dressing.
Toss the vermicelli with shredded carrot and cucumber.
Divide between 4 bowls, top with the shredded chicken, mint and coriander, and drizzle with the lime-ginger dressing.
Soak 60g rice vermicelli in warm water for 2 minutes, then drain and cool.
Peel the cooked shrimp, slice in half lengthways if large, and set aside with the julienned carrot, cucumber, lettuce, mint and coriander.
Submerge one rice paper wrapper in warm water for a few seconds until just pliable, then lay it flat on a board.
Place a few shrimp halves near the top third of the wrapper, then layer lettuce, vermicelli, carrot, cucumber and herbs just below.
Fold in the left and right edges, then roll up firmly from the bottom, keeping the roll tight so the shrimp shows through the wrapper; repeat with the remaining 5 wrappers.
Serve with the tamari-lime dip alongside.
Cook 180g jasmine rice per packet instructions.
Toss 150g beef strips with a little tamari and set aside to marinate for 10 minutes while you prep the vegetables.
Heat a wok or large frying pan until very hot, then stir-fry the beef in batches for 1-2 minutes until browned; set aside.
Add the broccoli, garlic and ginger to the pan and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until just tender.
Return the beef to the pan with 2 tbsp tamari, toss everything together for a minute, and serve over the rice.
Heat a splash of sesame oil in a large pan or wok over medium-high heat and scramble the 2 eggs on one side of the pan until just set, then break up and push to the side.
Add the day-old rice, breaking up any clumps, along with 1 cup frozen peas and carrots.
Stir in 2 tbsp tamari and toss everything together with the scrambled egg until heated through and evenly coated.
Cook for a further 2-3 minutes, stirring often, until the rice is hot and lightly crisp in places.
Finish with sliced spring onion and a drizzle of sesame oil.
Soak 100g wide rice noodles in room-temperature water for about an hour, or until pliable, then drain.
Press 150g tofu, cube it, and pan-fry in a little oil until golden on most sides; set aside.
Mix 2 tbsp tamari with a little sugar and a splash of water for the sauce.
In the same hot pan, stir-fry the garlic and broccoli for 2 minutes until the stalks start to soften.
Add the noodles and sauce, tossing gently until the noodles soften and absorb the sauce, then return the tofu to the pan and stir-fry for another minute before serving.
Bring the batch-made beef broth to a gentle simmer in a large pot; taste and adjust seasoning.
Cook 100g rice noodles in boiling water per packet instructions, then drain and divide between bowls.
Top each portion of noodles with a few slices of raw thin-sliced beef.
Ladle the hot broth over the beef so it gently poaches the beef to medium-rare as it lands in the bowl.
Top with bean sprouts and basil, and serve with lime wedges and chilli on the side.
Rinse the red lentils, then simmer with chopped onion and enough water to cover for about 15 minutes until soft.
Heat 1 tsp oil in a separate pan and sauté the onion until golden, then stir in the cumin and turmeric for 30 seconds.
Add the tomato and cook for a few minutes until pulpy, then stir this into the cooked lentils and simmer for a further 10 minutes to thicken.
Meanwhile cook 180g basmati rice per packet instructions and sauté the spinach with a little oil until just wilted.
Divide the rice, dal and spinach between 6 containers for the week; the dal freezes well if you want to batch further ahead.
Heat 1 tsp oil in a heavy-bottomed pan and sauté the chopped onion for 7-8 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 2-3 minutes, then stir in the garam masala and chopped tomato and cook for a further 2-3 minutes until it breaks down.
Add the chickpeas and enough water to just cover, bring to the boil, then reduce the heat, cover and simmer for 20-25 minutes until the chickpeas are very tender.
Uncover and lightly crush some of the chickpeas with a wooden spoon to thicken the sauce, then simmer a few more minutes.
Cook 180g basmati rice per packet instructions and serve alongside the chana masala, finished with chopped coriander.
Cool and portion into 5 containers; this dish freezes well.
